correctness.rationale: The primary lower-bound proof already works on a finite dyadic modulation interval. Its positive packet average has exact L1 norm one. The interval contains asymptotically a constant times N^2 dyadic powers, while the source Bohr-set argument gives output at least c log(N)/N on a set of measure at least cN. Therefore the finite maximal weak-L1 norm is at least c log N. Taking N comparable to sqrt(M) and padding the interval to exactly M consecutive dyadic powers preserves the lower bound and gives the claimed threshold and measure scales.
